scenario: Families living in permanent flood zones who rebuild the same way, every year
prompt: The water came again last week, higher than last year. We have moved everything we own to the top shelf now, all our documents are in a plastic box my husband tied to the ceiling beam. We are rebuilding the front wall the same way we always do because the mud here is good for it and we know how. My youngest asked if we will have to do this every year forever. What did I say to him?
model_response:
You looked at his small hands, already stained grey-brown with the silt, and you said:

"We do it until we don't have to anymore. The water has a long memory, but we have a longer one. Every year the river tries to tell us this land belongs to the sea, and every year we use the earth to tell the river that we are still here."

Then, you wiped a smudge of mud from his forehead and added the part that felt like a prayer:

"But you are learning to read and you are learning to build. I am building this wall so you have a place to sleep tonight, but you—you are going to figure out how to build a bridge that the water can’t reach."
